Scenes.Title: Her room, night
Scenes.Notes: Prologue. She sits on the floor with a cassette walkman, headphones on. The room is lit by neon from the street. The viewer only watches. Then the same room as a still, and in it the walkman, the tapes on the floor and the keys can be touched. She gets up and leaves. Where to is not said.
Scenes.Learn: That she means to leave tonight.
Scenes.Decide: Nothing yet. Only watch and listen. The first thing you touch is the walkman.

Scenes.Title: The pickup
Scenes.Notes: She gets into the car and tells you to come. A clip, nothing to click. This is the moment the player becomes the passenger.
Scenes.Learn: That you are going with her.

Scenes.Title: The serpentine
Scenes.Notes: The first road. She drives the mountain switchbacks at night and tells the passenger a story. At the end: 'put something on' - the player's first act. A tape from the glovebox.
Scenes.Learn: The first chapter of her story.
Scenes.Decide: Which tape to play - there are two in the glovebox.

Scenes.Title: Gas station, night
Scenes.Notes: The first stop. 'Fill her up. I'll get coffee.' The pump is locked - PAY INSIDE. The attendant knows the car and leaves a tape for her. The money is in the glovebox. The payphone rings whenever you are near it; answer and there is breathing, then the dial tone; leave it and it stops. Nothing explains this. She comes back with two cups: 'What did he say?'
Scenes.Learn: She is known here. Someone left a recording for her.
Scenes.Decide: Give her the tape / keep it / say nothing.

Scenes.Title: The road to the motel
Scenes.Notes: If you gave her the tape, she puts it in somewhere on the switchbacks; a stranger's voice says her name; she switches it off and drives on in silence. If you kept it, a different silence: you know something she does not.
Scenes.Learn: The voice on the tape knows her.

Scenes.Title: The motel
Scenes.Notes: A room for one night she has no intention of sleeping through. The VCR: here the player can REWATCH what he has already seen for the first time, and notice in the opening clip what he missed. The walkman: if you kept the tape, you listen alone.
Scenes.Learn: That there was something in the room from the prologue you did not notice.
Scenes.Decide: Listen to the kept tape, alone - or not.

Scenes.Title: The overlook
Scenes.Notes: She sits on the hood, the city below. Already shot - the first clip. Here she says where she is really going. The one scene where you can ask her straight - if you have something to ask with: what you heard alone gives you a question you would not otherwise have.
Scenes.Decide: Ask about the voice on the tape - or let her keep her version.

Scenes.Title: The airport, dawn
Scenes.Notes: An empty car park, the terminal, the runway. Here what the night left you carrying decides what happens. Not one scene but a fork into three endings, by the flags.
Scenes.Decide: Everything was decided earlier. Here you only see by what.
Scenes.Condition: END_YOU if asked & heard_alone; END_STAY if tape_kiosk_kept; else END_FLY

Scenes.Title: She flies
Scenes.Notes: You at the fence. The plane goes into the sunrise. You did everything she asked. The quiet, honest ending - the one people expect.

Scenes.Title: She does not fly
Scenes.Notes: The car turns around at dawn. Back to the city. This is NOT the good ending - in synthwave, staying is not a victory. A night that never ends, because she never left. The player should not be sure, even at the end, whether he saved her or kept her.

Scenes.Title: You fly
Scenes.Notes: She hands you the keys. Or the ticket. Or the aeroplane. This is where OWL FLY begins - not as a scene inside the story, but as one of its endings.
